options.C: Regressive

explanation: Spot on! Exercising and leaning on a support system are classic healthy, adaptive ways to handle pressure.

question: What is the primary role of the nurse during the implementation phase?

options.A: Taking over all physical labor so locals do not work
options.B: Writing laws to force people to attend health clinics
options.C: Sitting in an office away from the project site
options.D: Providing technical guidance and supporting community action

explanation: Nurses act as facilitators and technical guides while the community executes the planned health interventions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why is maintaining good hydration especially vital for a bedbound person?

options.A: It replaces the need for physical therapy
options.B: It completely cures physical paralysis over time
options.C: It prevents dehydration that can damage skin integrity
options.D: It stops the patient from feeling hungry

explanation: Adequate fluids keep the skin elastic and well-perfused, reducing the risk of pressure injuries and breakdown. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h4)

question: What is the medical term for a fit?

options.A: Spasm
options.B: Stroke
options.C: Seizure
options.D: Syncope

explanation: A fit is medically referred to as a seizure, which involves abnormal electrical activity in the brain. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h1)

question: Two senior nurses are arguing bitterly over shift schedules, and the manager encourages both to give up a preferred off-day to meet in the middle. Which style is this?

options.A: Avoiding
options.B: Competing
options.C: Compromise
options.D: Collaboration

explanation: Compromise requires each person to concede something, resulting in a shared middle ground where neither gets everything they wanted. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h7)

question: What is the main goal of advance care planning discussions?

options.A: Reducing overall hospital financial costs for end-of-life care
options.B: Transferring legal responsibility entirely to the nursing staff
options.C: Convincing the patient to sign a do-not-resuscitate order immediately
options.D: Aligning future medical treatments with the patient's personal values

explanation: Advance care planning ensures that future medical care reflects what the patient truly values and wants. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h5)

question: Which nursing action directly supports antimicrobial stewardship?

options.A: Advocating to collect culture specimens before starting antibiotics
options.B: Giving leftover antibiotics to a family member with a cold
options.C: Requesting broad-spectrum drugs for every routine fever
options.D: Stopping antibiotic therapy as soon as mild symptoms improve

explanation: Getting cultures first ensures the right targeted drug is used, preventing unnecessary use of broad-spectrum medications. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h4)

question: A patient is brought in bleeding heavily from a leg wound and gasping for air. Following the ABCDE approach, what should you address first?

options.A: Ask the patient for their home address and phone number
options.B: Ensure a patent airway and check breathing
options.C: Clean the leg wound with antiseptic solution
options.D: Document the exact time of the injury in the chart

explanation: Airway and breathing always come first in the ABCDE sequence—even before stopping severe bleeding in circulation! Think A-B-C.

question: What is the most common cause of salpingitis?

options.A: Sexually transmitted bacteria
options.B: Autoimmune joint disorders
options.C: Fungal overgrowth from antibiotics
options.D: Congenital structural defects

explanation: Infections like Chlamydia and Gonorrhea are the main culprits behind most fallopian tube infections.

question: What is a common nutrition mistake people make when switching to packaged gluten-free foods?

options.A: Consuming too much natural protein from fresh fruits and vegetables
options.B: Eating too many processed substitutes lacking fiber and B vitamins
options.C: Developing an immediate intolerance to all dairy products
options.D: Suffering from severe protein toxicity due to meat overconsumption

explanation: It's easy to rely on packaged gluten-free snacks, but many lack the fiber and vitamins found in whole or fortified foods.

question: How is a nursing audit different from a general staff performance appraisal?

options.A: Audits are done only by doctors, while appraisals are done by senior nurses
options.B: Audits deal with hospital finances, while appraisals deal with patient beds
options.C: Audits happen daily, while appraisals happen only once in a lifetime
options.D: Audits focus on patient care processes, while appraisals focus on overall staff conduct

explanation: Great thinking! A performance appraisal looks at how a nurse behaves on the job overall, while an audit zooms in specifically on clinical care and nursing records.

question: How should you as a nurse organize your questions when running through a review of systems?

options.A: Let the patient talk freely without any guided direction
options.B: Ask targeted questions system by system from head to toe
options.C: Ask the patient to list every illness they had as a child
options.D: Focus only on the exact organ system of the main complaint

explanation: Brilliant! Going step-by-step from the head down ensures you never accidentally leave out an important body system.

question: Why is relying on informal personal shortcuts instead of established hospital policy dangerous?

options.A: It forces the hospital to buy expensive new computer systems
options.B: It creates inconsistency and increases the risk of medical errors
options.C: It automatically increases the nurse's monthly salary
options.D: It saves too much time and makes nursing look too easy

explanation: Informal shortcuts bypass vital safety checks, leading to unpredictable care quality and a higher chance of making a mistake.

question: What is the main medical benefit of giving zinc supplements during childhood diarrhoea?

options.A: It instantly stops all vomiting within one hour
options.B: It replaces lost potassium in the bloodstream
options.C: It repairs the gut lining and shortens illness duration
options.D: It acts as a strong painkiller for stomach cramps

explanation: Zinc is wonderful for healing! It acts like medicine for the gut walls, helping them repair faster and boosting the child's immune system to clear the bug away.

question: Which of the following is NOT a goal of identifying FGM in a clinical setting?

options.A: Protecting younger female siblings from undergoing the practice
options.B: Anticipating and preparing for potential obstetric complications
options.C: Publicly shaming the family in the hospital waiting room
options.D: Providing appropriate referrals for psychological support

explanation: Nurses never shame or punish families! Our job is to provide clinical care, educate, offer support, and protect vulnerable children. Keep up the stellar work!

question: Which physical factor is most essential for keeping waterborne diseases out of a neighborhood?

options.A: Multistory housing units with elevators
options.B: Wide concrete roads for vehicle traffic
options.C: Large recreational parks with green spaces
options.D: Consistent access to safe, clean drinking water

explanation: Spot on! Clean water is our absolute best shield against nasty bugs like cholera and typhoid.

question: A local government wants nurses to happily stay long-term in remote health posts. Which step is most effective?

options.A: Reducing the operational hours of remote clinics to twice a week
options.B: Threatening to dismiss any nurse who requests a transfer to an urban center
options.C: Eliminating all training programs to keep staff working on site full-time
options.D: Providing staff quarters, hardship allowances, and regular promotion opportunities

explanation: Taking care of staff needs—like providing a place to live and rewarding their hard work—makes them want to stay and serve the community.

question: Why are anthropometric measurements so helpful in busy or rural primary healthcare clinics?

options.A: They replace the need for taking a complete medical history
options.B: They are non-invasive, affordable, and simple to perform anywhere
options.C: They require expensive laboratory reagents to process results
options.D: They provide instant diagnosis for all known infectious diseases

explanation: Spot on! Because they need very little equipment and no lab work, you can easily use them during community outreaches or rural postings.

question: Where do we usually place a peripheral arterial line?

options.A: Carotid artery
options.B: Radial artery
options.C: Femoral vein
options.D: Brachial vein

explanation: The radial artery at the wrist is our go-to spot because it is easy to reach and has great backup blood supply (collateral circulation).

question: A public health nurse distributes insecticide-treated nets to families in a rural malaria-endemic village. Which prevention strategy is this?

options.A: Primordial legislation
options.B: Specific protection
options.C: Tertiary rehabilitation
options.D: Secondary screening

explanation: Using bed nets protects specific individuals directly from mosquito bites and malaria transmission, fitting under specific protection. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h2)

question: A patient comes to the clinic with ongoing pelvic pain and high anxiety, and hints point toward past abuse. What does this show us?

options.A: That physical injuries from violence always heal completely in a few weeks
options.B: That mental health struggles never cause physical pain in the body
options.C: That chronic physical symptoms and emotional trauma are often connected
options.D: That the patient is just making up symptoms to get drugs

explanation: Spot on! Violence often leaves lasting physical pain right alongside deep emotional scars, which is why holistic nursing care is so important.

question: Which of these is NOT a standard community prevention message taught by nurses?

options.A: Attending antenatal clinics for preventive treatment during pregnancy
options.B: Sleeping inside insecticide-treated nets every single night
options.C: Taking high doses of antibiotics to prevent malaria infection
options.D: Clearing stagnant water puddles around residential houses

explanation: Correct! Antibiotics fight bacteria, not malaria parasites. Taking them for malaria is incorrect and only builds drug resistance.

question: Which method is best when teaching a community with low literacy levels?

options.A: Giving long lectures without any visual props or pictures
options.B: Using visual aids, drama, and group demonstrations
options.C: Writing detailed medical prescriptions on the chalkboard
options.D: Distributing dense scientific textbooks to every household

explanation: Correct! Pictures, role-play, and practical demos bypass reading barriers and make health messages fun and easy to grasp.

question: How does a shortage of nursing staff directly impact patient care in a hospital?

options.A: It reduces patient waiting times in the emergency room.
options.B: It increases staff workloads and raises the risk of burnout and errors.
options.C: It automatically improves the quality of surgical procedures.
options.D: It ensures that every patient gets private room nursing.

explanation: Fewer nurses handling high numbers of patients leads to physical exhaustion, mental burnout, and mistakes that threaten patient safety. [learn more](GST322_U3_T7#GST322_U3_T7_h4)

question: Which of these nursing actions is a good example of primary disease prevention?

options.A: Administering the measles vaccine to an infant
options.B: Screening adults for high blood pressure
options.C: Treating complications of chronic stroke
options.D: Isolating a patient with active tuberculosis

explanation: You got it! Primary prevention stops a disease before it even starts—and immunizations are the classic example.

question: Why is teaching the community so important for getting rid of infection reservoirs long-term?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any professional medical personnel
options.B: It empowers local residents to sustain hygiene and sanitation practices independently
options.C: It replaces the scientific need for laboratory testing and animal vaccines
options.D: It ensures that infectious pathogens mutate into harmless environmental plants

explanation: When people understand the 'why' behind healthy habits, they keep practicing good hygiene long after healthcare workers pack up and leave. Community power!

question: A patient with lung cancer is still getting chemotherapy while also receiving care for severe pain and shortness of breath. What kind of approach is this?

options.A: Integrating palliative care alongside curative treatment
options.B: Treating the side effects of chemotherapy exclusively with surgery
options.C: Abandoning curative treatment in favor of hospice
options.D: Stopping all medical interventions to allow natural death

explanation: Brilliant! Patients don't have to choose just one. They can receive treatments to fight the illness (like chemotherapy) while simultaneously getting comfort care to manage their symptoms.

question: Which vaccine is especially vital for healthcare workers who handle medical waste and sharps?

options.A: Hepatitis B vaccine
options.B: Rabies immunization
options.C: Yellow fever vaccine
options.D: Tetanus toxoid booster

explanation: Hepatitis B is a serious blood-borne virus easily spread through accidental needle-sticks, making vaccination essential for healthcare staff. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h8)

question: What is the best position for a patient during a thoracocentesis?

options.A: Lying flat on their stomach with the head turned to the side
options.B: Lying flat on their back with arms straight down
options.C: Sitting upright and leaning forward over a bedside table
options.D: Standing upright against a rigid wall with eyes closed

explanation: This posture widens the spaces between the ribs, making it safer and easier to insert the needle. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h3)

question: What standard unit of measurement is used on a hospital fluid intake and output chart?

options.A: Kilograms
options.B: Liters
options.C: Milliliters
options.D: Ounces

explanation: Milliliters provide the precise detail needed to track small fluid shifts safely. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h6)

question: Why were some people initially hesitant about modern family planning programs in Nigeria?

options.A: A total lack of trained nurses in every region of the country
options.B: Strict government bans on building hospitals and clinics
options.C: Cultural norms, religious beliefs, and mistrust of population policies
options.D: The complete absence of traditional birth spacing methods

explanation: Because these programs were newly introduced, many communities viewed them with suspicion, worrying about foreign population control motives.

question: What is the main purpose of a long white cane for mobility?

options.A: To detect ground-level obstacles and uneven surfaces ahead
options.B: To measure the exact distance between walls in a room
options.C: To provide a sturdy walking frame for lower body weakness
options.D: To signal healthcare workers to administer eye medications

explanation: Think of the white cane as an extra helper that sweeps the floor ahead, warning the user about curbs, steps, and obstacles in their path.

question: What is the common clinical name for Pelvic Floor Muscle Training exercises?

options.A: Abdominal crunches
options.B: Lamaze breathing
options.C: Pelvic tilt maneuvers
options.D: Kegel exercises

explanation: Easy peasy! Kegels are the go-to exercises we teach patients to tone and rebuild their pelvic strength.

question: Why do we encourage regular walking for patients with stable Peripheral Artery Disease?

options.A: It lowers the total volume of blood circulating in the body.
options.B: It immediately dissolves any deep vein blood clots in the legs.
options.C: It helps develop collateral blood vessels around blocked arteries.
options.D: It forces existing fatty plaque out through the capillary bed.

explanation: Exercise is amazing here! Gentle walking encourages the body to build tiny 'detour roads' (collateral vessels) to bypass the blocked main arteries.

question: What is the purpose of an EMR audit trail?

options.A: To automatically record every time a user opens or views a patient chart
options.B: To measure how fast a patient recovers from surgery
options.C: To monitor how many steps a nurse walks during a 12-hour shift
options.D: To track how much money the hospital spends on computer maintenance

explanation: An audit trail leaves a digital footprint, tracking who looked at a patient's file and exactly when they opened it.

question: When is the risk of getting pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) highest after an IUD insertion?

options.A: Only if the client gets pregnant with the IUD
options.B: During the first 20 days after insertion
options.C: There is never any risk of infection
options.D: After the IUD has been in place for five years

explanation: Because tiny amounts of bacteria can accidentally enter the uterus during the procedure, the infection risk is highest right after insertion, during the first few weeks.

question: What are the bumpy swellings on autonomic nerve fibers that release chemicals onto smooth muscle called?

options.A: Dense bodies
options.B: Motor end plates
options.C: Synaptic knobs
options.D: Varicosities

explanation: Instead of neat little single connections, autonomic nerves have string-of-pearls swellings called varicosities that spray neurotransmitters across a wider area. Neat, right?

question: When a nurse uses skinfold calipers, which specific layer of tissue are they measuring?

options.A: Visceral fat
options.B: Subcutaneous fat
options.C: Deep fascia
options.D: Skeletal muscle

explanation: Correct! Calipers pinch and measure the layer of fat that lives right underneath the skin (subcutaneous fat).

question: Why must you always ask patients about any herbal remedies they take alongside prescription drugs?

options.A: Some herbs can dangerously alter the effects of prescribed medications
options.B: Traditional plants always neutralize standard hospital equipment
options.C: Herbal remedies are illegal to consume in any home care setting
options.D: Doctors refuse to document any natural products in the chart

explanation: Spot on! Herbs are active substances. Mixing them with hospital drugs can accidentally boost or block the medication, causing dangerous side effects.

question: What is actually happening inside the body during the incubation period of an infectious disease?

options.A: Early, non-specific fatigue and body aches first start to show
options.B: The patient experiences the peak physical signs of the illness
options.C: Acute symptoms fade and body tissues begin to repair themselves
options.D: The pathogen multiplies inside the body without causing symptoms

explanation: You nailed it! During the incubation period, the germs have entered and are quietly throwing a party inside, multiplying until there are enough to finally make the patient feel sick.

question: Why is advocating for good patient nutrition such a big deal in modern nursing?

options.A: Nurses are required by law to cook meals for every patient
options.B: It generates extra revenue for the hospital administration
options.C: Proper nutrition is essential for preventing and managing chronic diseases
options.D: It replaces the need for administering prescribed medications

explanation: Good food is medicine! Helping patients get the right nutrients speeds up their healing and keeps chronic illnesses under control.

question: An exposed person stays completely healthy past the maximum known incubation period for that bug. What can you safely conclude as a nurse?

options.A: The person is now immune for the rest of their life
options.B: The pathogen has entered a permanent latent stage
options.C: The person did not contract the infection from the exposure
options.D: The quarantine period must be doubled just to be safe

explanation: Correct! If no symptoms show up within the maximum window, it means they dodged the infection.

question: About how much does a normal pregnant woman's total blood volume increase?

options.A: 5 percent
options.B: 100 percent
options.C: 10 percent
options.D: 50 percent

explanation: Amazing right? The body ramps up blood volume by about half to care for both the mother and the growing baby. That's why iron and fluids are so crucial!

question: What is a common reason why people strictly follow food taboos?

options.A: Direct orders from national medical boards
options.B: Lack of physical transport to farms
options.C: High market prices for the forbidden foods
options.D: Fear of social disapproval, curses, or bad luck

explanation: Taboos are tied to deep spiritual beliefs, so people worry about negative social or supernatural consequences if they break the rules.

question: Why is washing out the stomach (gastric lavage) rarely recommended nowadays for routine poisoning cases?

options.A: Lavage only works if the patient drank pure alcohol or petroleum products.
options.B: Activated charcoal completely replaces the need for any physical stomach cleaning.
options.C: The procedure carries significant risks of aspiration and mechanical injury to the esophagus.
options.D: Stomach contents empty into the small intestine within seconds of swallowing.

explanation: Passing a thick tube down into the stomach can easily cause bleeding, injury, or worse—pushing the poison into the lungs. That's why we rely on safer methods now!

question: Why is an intramuscular injection of Vitamin K given routinely to all newborns?

options.A: To prevent dangerous bleeding disorders
options.B: To boost immediate antibody production
options.C: To treat congenital eye infections
options.D: To protect against bacterial meningitis

explanation: Newborn guts are sterile and cannot make Vitamin K yet, so an injection stops life-threatening bleeding complications. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h7)

question: What is the main goal of Post-Abortion Care (PAC) in our healthcare settings?

options.A: To reduce maternal illness and death from unsafe abortions
options.B: To enforce strict population control policies in hospitals
options.C: To promote voluntary pregnancy termination in rural clinics
options.D: To provide free antenatal care for pregnant teenagers

explanation: You've got this! PAC is an emergency strategy put in place to lower the high rates of death and sickness caused by unsafe abortion complications.

question: Which type of graph is best suited for showing continuous data tracked over time?

options.A: Scatter table
options.B: Line graph
options.C: Demographic matrix
options.D: Pie chart

explanation: Line graphs are specifically designed to illustrate trends and changes across sequential time points. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is a key nursing duty to help prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia?

options.A: Giving strong antibiotics to every intubated patient
options.B: Keeping the head of the bed completely flat
options.C: Changing the ventilator machine every hour
options.D: Performing regular oral care with antiseptic solutions

explanation: Mouth hygiene is huge! Keeping the mouth clean stops nasty bacteria from multiplying and sliding down into the lungs.

question: Why must quality assurance decisions be data-driven rather than based on guesswork?

options.A: Data collection completely eliminates all human error
options.B: Data provides accurate proof of where problems exist and if changes actually work
options.C: Hospital management only accepts reports written in numbers
options.D: Guesswork is illegal for registered nurses in Nigeria

explanation: In nursing, we rely on facts! Real data gives us clear proof of what's going wrong and whether our new ideas are actually fixing the problem.

question: Which antiseptic is most commonly used to clean the skin before putting in a cannula?

options.A: Hydrogen peroxide
options.B: Plain tap water
options.C: Chlorhexidine
options.D: Sterile mineral oil

explanation: Chlorhexidine is our go-to skin cleaner for stopping germs and keeping nasty bloodstream infections away.

question: Which test is primarily used to check if a female patient's fallopian tubes are open and clear?

options.A: Testicular biopsy
options.B: Semen analysis
options.C: Hysterosalpingography
options.D: Basal body temperature graphing

question: What is the best approach for managing pain in an infant who has just been circumcised?

options.A: Applying ice packs directly to the bare surgical wound for hours
options.B: Administering strong opioid medications every two hours around the clock
options.C: Keeping the infant awake so they do not feel the post-surgical pain
options.D: Using sweet oral sucrose solution alongside prescribed mild pain relievers

explanation: Sweet sucrose drops combined with safe, mild pain meds (like paracetamol) provide great comfort and pain relief for babies.

question: A colleague asks to quickly log in under your computer account because they forgot their password. What should you do?

options.A: Complete the charting for them under your own name instead
options.B: Refuse and ask them to log in using their own credentials
options.C: Allow them to type quickly while you watch over their shoulder
options.D: Write your password down on a sticky note for them to use later

explanation: Always keep your login secure! Sharing it means you take the blame for whatever gets charted on that account.

question: A clinic nurse notices that teen mothers are frequently turned away because they lack funds for registration. Which core principle is being violated?

options.A: Equitability
options.B: Technical competence
options.C: Confidentiality
options.D: Appropriateness

explanation: Equitability means healthcare is delivered fairly to all young people regardless of their social status or ability to pay. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T4#GNS312_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the correct emergency action if a patient takes a sublingual nitroglycerin tablet and their chest pain doesn't go away?

options.A: Wait five minutes, take a second tablet, and call for emergency help if needed
options.B: Take a deep breath and continue the physical exercise they were doing
options.C: Wait twenty minutes for the medicine to absorb before doing anything else
options.D: Swallow three tablets at once immediately and lie flat on the floor

explanation: The golden rule for nitro is: take one tablet every 5 minutes (up to 3 total). If pain persists after the very first one, call emergency services right away!

question: What is the main goal of conducting a community health assessment?

options.A: To gather data on population health needs and available resources
options.B: To close down clinics that do not meet modern standards
options.C: To prescribe individual drugs to every household member
options.D: To punish local leaders for poor sanitation practices

explanation: Spot on! Before a nurse can help a community, they must first find out what problems exist and what resources are already available.

question: What happens when a nurse falls into 'confirmation bias' during clinical assessment?

options.A: Forgetting to check vital signs because of a sudden emergency
options.B: Trusting equipment alarms even when they are making false noises
options.C: Blaming a coworker for a mistake you made during a procedure
options.D: Looking only for signs that prove your first guess and ignoring others

explanation: You got it! Confirmation bias is when our brain only looks for clues that match our very first thought about what is wrong, while ignoring other important signs.

question: Which simple tool do nurses use right in the field to quickly check if a child is suffering from malnutrition?

options.A: A pulse oximeter
options.B: A standard blood pressure cuff
options.C: Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) tape
options.D: A peak flow meter

explanation: The colorful MUAC tape is a nurse's best friend in community outreaches and disaster zones for spotting malnutrition in seconds.

question: What is the primary goal of conducting regular nursing assessments in an adult day care setting?

options.A: To establish health baselines and catch subtle changes early
options.B: To enforce strict institutional rules upon the clients
options.C: To diagnose complex mental health disorders independently
options.D: To permanently replace the client's primary care physician

explanation: Regular assessments help nurses monitor chronic conditions and identify early signs of physical or cognitive deterioration before they become acute emergencies. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary local physical effect of applying warmth via a poultice?

options.A: Permanent darkening of the skin
options.B: Immediate freezing of skin cells
options.C: Complete blockage of local blood flow
options.D: Vasodilation of local blood vessels

question: Which type of exercise involves the nurse moving the joints of a patient who cannot move at all?

options.A: Passive exercises
options.B: Resistive exercises
options.C: Active exercises
options.D: Active-assistive exercises

explanation: When a patient cannot move their limbs themselves, you step in and gently move their joints for them. That is what passive exercises are all about!

question: Why is getting feedback or follow-up from regulators after submitting an ADR report helpful?

options.A: It calculates the financial fine that the hospital must pay
options.B: It cancels the patient's original prescription record
options.C: It serves as a formal warning letter to discipline the reporting nurse
options.D: It helps clarify missing details and shares broader safety updates with clinicians

explanation: Follow-ups aren't punishments! They help ensure our report is accurate and share important safety updates back with healthcare workers.

question: A nurse wants to find articles about asthma in children, but wants to completely leave out studies on adults. Which search string is best?

options.A: asthma NOT children AND adults
options.B: asthma AND children AND adults
options.C: asthma AND children NOT adults
options.D: asthma OR children OR adults

question: Which factor represents part of the physical school health environment?

options.A: Safe water supply and clean toilets
options.B: The political climate of the community
options.C: The emotional stability of the principal
options.D: The grading system used for examinations

explanation: Physical components refer to tangible structures and amenities like safe drinking water, ventilation, and sanitation facilities. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why does iron-deficiency anemia often leave a person feeling completely wiped out?

options.A: Low iron directly destroys the motor neurons in the spinal cord.

options.C: The body must burn excessive calories to manufacture extra platelets.
options.D: Anemia causes an immediate and permanent drop in blood pressure.
