question: Why are notifiable disease registers important for public health authorities?

options.A: They calculate the monthly salary of hospital staff
options.B: They track legally reportable infections to protect the public
options.C: They replace the need for patient physical examinations
options.D: They determine which patients get discharged first

explanation: Registers keep a formal record of dangerous infections that require immediate public health action. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h4)

question: What is the main goal of medical asepsis?

options.A: To eliminate every single microbial spore in the room
options.B: To sterilize surgical instruments before an operation
options.C: To reduce the number of pathogens and prevent their spread
options.D: To treat active bacterial infections with strong antibiotics

explanation: Medical asepsis focuses on keeping germ numbers low using clean techniques like handwashing to stop disease spread. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the teach-back method used for during patient education?

options.A: Having the patient explain instructions in their own words
options.B: Reviewing textbook chapters with the family caregiver
options.C: Allowing the patient to teach nursing students clinical skills
options.D: Testing the patient's long-term memory after a stroke

explanation: The teach-back method requires patients to repeat back what they understood, confirming they actually grasped the instructions. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h5)

question: During discharge planning, which hospital professional do nurses commonly work with to help a patient's financial needs?

options.A: Hospital maintenance engineers
options.B: Medical social workers
options.C: Pharmaceutical sales reps
options.D: IT staff

explanation: Medical social workers are our best friends when it comes to connecting patients with welfare, charity funds, and community support!

question: What is the main reason developing countries experience more complications from unsafe injections?

options.A: A complete lack of trained nurses in regional clinics
options.B: Patients refusing oral medications in favor of injections
options.C: The natural resistance of tropical germs to standard soap
options.D: Supply shortages and poor waste management systems

explanation: Exactly. When clinics struggle with equipment shortages, it can unfortunately lead to dangerous workarounds like reusing syringes. You're building great clinical awareness! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is a major perk of using a pie chart in a presentation?

options.A: They automatically correct data collection errors
options.B: They can display unlimited categories without clutter
options.C: They are easily understood by non-scientific audiences
options.D: They are the only graph type accepted in research journals

explanation: That's right! Even people outside of healthcare can glance at a pie chart and instantly get the picture.

question: Why is the muscular wall of the left ventricle thicker than the right ventricle?

options.A: It holds a larger volume of blood
options.B: It gets blood directly from the lungs under high pressure
options.C: It pumps blood through the whole body against high pressure
options.D: It beats much faster than the right side

explanation: Think of it this way: the left side has to push blood all the way to your toes and fingers, while the right side only goes to the nearby lungs. More distance means it needs more muscle power!

question: Which type of study focuses on describing the person, place, and time of a disease outbreak?

options.A: Surgical audit
options.B: Analytical study
options.C: Clinical trial
options.D: Descriptive study

explanation: Correct! Descriptive studies simply paint the picture of who is sick, where they are, and when it happened. You're crushing it!

question: What is a major risk if a low-calorie diet lacks essential vitamins and minerals?

options.A: Permanent loss of the sense of taste
options.B: Nutritional deficiencies and fatigue
options.C: Rapid increase in bone mineral density
options.D: Sudden enlargement of the thyroid gland

explanation: Spot on! Eating less food overall means you might miss out on vital nutrients, which commonly leads to feeling constantly tired and run-down.

question: Which scenario best demonstrates the function of sensory association areas?

options.A: Recognizing a hot cup of tea by its steam, warmth, and aroma together
options.B: Feeling a sharp pinprick on the skin and pulling the hand away quickly
options.C: Hearing a loud sudden sound and turning the head toward the noise
options.D: Blinking automatically when a bright light flashes in front of the eyes

explanation: Recognizing an object by combining multiple sensory cues like sight, temperature, and smell requires sensory association areas. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T11#GNS211_U3_T11_h7)

question: Why might someone with noticeable facial scarification face social challenges today?

options.A: Their immune system will completely shut down
options.B: They may experience social stigma and discrimination
options.C: They will lose the ability to speak clearly
options.D: Their body will automatically develop chronic malaria

explanation: Spot on. Shifting societal views and modern settings can sometimes lead to unfair judgment against visibly marked individuals, impacting their peace of mind.

question: Who is the main target group for the preventive HPV vaccine?

options.A: Young adolescent girls before sexual debut
options.B: Infants during their routine immunization schedule
options.C: Elderly women over the age of sixty-five
options.D: Adult men diagnosed with chronic prostatitis

explanation: Spot on! The vaccine works best when given to young girls before they are ever exposed to HPV.

question: Why are overfilled sharps containers dangerous on the ward?

options.A: They attract insects and rodents into patient care areas
options.B: They release toxic chemical fumes into the nursing station
options.C: They expose workers to protruding needles and unstable sharp items
options.D: They prevent the automated counting of used syringes

explanation: Once a sharps box is past its fill line, needles start stacking up near the top and can easily prick the next person trying to dispose of waste. Close them on time!

question: Who acts as the main health bridge between the school, the family, and local clinics?

options.A: The school security guard
options.B: The school accountant
options.C: The sports coach
options.D: The school nurse

explanation: Correct! The school nurse handles health needs, talks with parents, and connects sick children to nearby health clinics.

question: How do most patients typically approach HIV disclosure?

options.A: By printing flyers and distributing them in the local market
options.B: By refusing to ever tell anyone under any circumstance
options.C: Selectively, by telling specific trusted individuals over time
options.D: By announcing it publicly to their entire workplace on day one

explanation: Disclosure is usually a gradual, graded process where patients share their status only with carefully chosen people. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h4)

question: A village starts the year with no cholera, but 10 people fall sick by March. What do these 10 new cases represent?

options.A: The recovery rate of the infected population
options.B: The prevalence of cholera in the village
options.C: The mortality rate of the disease outbreak
options.D: The incidence of cholera for that period

explanation: Because these 10 folks developed the illness during that time window, they are the brand-new cases—making it the incidence!

question: Which of these is a main dietary goal for preventing lifestyle diseases?

options.A: Eliminating all forms of protein from meals
options.B: Reducing excessive salt and sugar intake
options.C: Doubling daily caloric consumption
options.D: Eating only imported canned foods

explanation: Spot on! Cutting down on too much salt and sugar is a powerful way to help prevent conditions like hypertension, obesity, and diabetes.

question: Why should nurses avoid cliché phrases like 'time heals all wounds' when talking to someone who is grieving?

options.A: It is scientifically incorrect according to modern psychology
options.B: It can minimize their pain and make them feel dismissed
options.C: It causes immediate physical regression into the denial stage
options.D: It violates standard nursing documentation guidelines

explanation: Spot on! Clichés can shut down honest communication because they make the person feel like their unique pain is being brushed aside.

question: Why do we treat a blood transfusion with the same high level of caution as an organ transplant?

options.A: It requires permanent immunosuppressive drug therapy
options.B: It can only be performed in major surgical theaters
options.C: It involves the total replacement of the patient's blood
options.D: It involves transferring living tissue that triggers immune responses

explanation: Think of donated blood as living tissue! When it enters a new body, the recipient's immune system will check it out and can spark a reaction if it doesn't match.

question: Which nursing action is most important when putting in a urinary catheter?

options.A: Inflating the retention balloon before inserting the tube
options.B: Lubricating only the very tip of the drainage collection bag
options.C: Applying heavy pressure to the lower abdomen while pushing
options.D: Maintaining strict sterile technique throughout the procedure

explanation: Keeping everything super sterile stops nasty germs from hitching a ride up into the bladder and causing a painful infection. Safety first in clinicals!

question: Which client is most at risk for having a very hard time adjusting after losing a spouse?

options.A: A client who anticipated the death for many years following a chronic illness
options.B: A client with limited social support who depended entirely on the spouse for daily functioning
options.C: A client who participates actively in a supportive religious community
options.D: A client who has successfully coped with multiple past life crises

explanation: Spot on! When someone relies completely on their partner and lacks a strong backup support system, the loss hits much harder and recovery is tougher.

question: A patient presents to the clinic reporting stool coming through her vagina two weeks after a difficult childbirth. What is the nurse's priority action during assessment?

options.A: Tell the patient this is a normal postpartum change that will resolve in a few days
options.B: Provide a gentle, empathetic history and prepare the patient for a careful physical examination
options.C: Perform a high-pressure enema to clear the bowel immediately
options.D: Immediately schedule the patient for emergency major surgery without further assessment

explanation: A sensitive history and gentle physical examination are essential to confirm the diagnosis and assess tissue health before planning treatment. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h4)

question: How does active immunization protect the body against future infections?

options.A: By destroying all existing white blood cells in the bloodstream
options.B: By transferring ready-made antibodies directly from another person
options.C: By stimulating the immune system to produce its own antibodies
options.D: By providing instant chemical disinfection on the skin surface

explanation: Active immunity acts like a gym workout for your immune system, teaching it to build its own antibodies and remember germs for later.

question: A patient with diabetes keeps sneaking traditional sugary snacks. What is the best first step for the nurse?

options.A: Report the patient to the medical team for non-compliance
options.B: Refuse to provide any further nursing care until they comply
options.C: Remove all personal food items from the bedside table
options.D: Respect their autonomy while calmly explaining the health risks

explanation: You're building great clinical judgment! Instead of policing or scolding, we respect their choice while gently teaching them why health risks matter. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h2)

question: A patient with type 2 diabetes needs help managing their meals. What is a great, simple tip to share first?

options.A: Replace all water intake with fresh vegetable juices only
options.B: Cook your vegetables without any seasoning or oil whatsoever
options.C: Stop eating all forms of food for two days of the week
options.D: Fill half of your meal plate with non-starchy, colorful vegetables

explanation: You nailed it! The plate method is a fantastic, visual way to help patients control portions and get enough fiber without stressful calorie counting.

question: During non-surgical care for a kidney injury, which nursing sign is most important to report immediately?

options.A: An increase in sleepiness after receiving a scheduled pain medication
options.B: Mild bruising fading to a yellow color around the flank area
options.C: A sudden drop in blood pressure paired with a fast heart rate
options.D: A slight yellow tinge in the normal daily urine output

explanation: A fast heart rate and dropping blood pressure are early warning signs of hidden internal bleeding. Catching this early can save a life!

question: What is a common health problem in children who eat a poor, low-diversity diet?

options.A: Complete immunity to common childhood tropical diseases
options.B: Rapid increase in bone density and excessive height
options.C: Sudden development of high blood pressure in infancy
options.D: Increased vulnerability to infections and stunted physical growth

explanation: That's right. Missing out on diverse nutrients weakens their immune system and slows down their growth, leading to frequent illnesses.

question: Which common local Nigerian vegetable is packed with iron, calcium, and vitamins for nursing mums?

options.A: Dried white table salt
options.B: Polished white rice
options.C: Fluted pumpkin leaves (ugu)
options.D: Refined wheat flour

explanation: Dark leafy greens like ugu are local nutrition powerhouses! They are packed with the iron and vitamins needed to recover well and boost milk production.

question: How is oligomenorrhoea different from amenorrhoea?

options.A: Oligomenorrhoea involves infrequent bleeding while amenorrhoea means complete absence of bleeding
options.B: Oligomenorrhoea occurs only in older women while amenorrhoea affects teenagers
options.C: Oligomenorrhoea causes heavy bleeding while amenorrhoea causes painful cramping
options.D: Oligomenorrhoea is a normal variant while amenorrhoea is always pathological

explanation: Nice and clear! Oligomenorrhoea means the periods happen, just less often (infrequent). Amenorrhoea means they have completely stopped (absence). Easy to remember for your exams!

question: What happens in a Type I error during research?

options.A: Rejecting a true null hypothesis, creating a false positive
options.B: Using a sample size that is far too large for the hospital ward
options.C: Failing to reject a false null hypothesis, creating a false negative
options.D: Forgetting to calculate the mean before publishing a research paper

explanation: A Type I error is like getting a false alarm—you mistakenly think your new intervention works wonders, but it's actually just random chance.

question: Why can't a nurse just study a huge, broad clinical topic without narrowing it down first?

options.A: It lacks the specific focus needed to collect and analyze relevant data
options.B: Patients will not want to participate in broad studies
options.C: Hospital management will refuse to fund broad topics
options.D: It is illegal to research topics that are too wide

explanation: If a topic is too wide (like 'malaria in Nigeria'), you won't know where to start looking. Narrowing it down helps you focus on exact details you can actually measure.

question: Which of these is NOT something a government agency typically does in the food supply chain?

options.A: Managing social safety nets like school feeding programs
options.B: Regulating the import and export of agricultural commodities
options.C: Setting retail prices for every independent restaurant in the country
options.D: Enforcing food safety standards and conducting health inspections

explanation: Governments check food safety and handle imports, but they don't micromanage what individual restaurants charge for a plate of food!

question: What is the main reason for involving community and religious leaders in youth health programs?

options.A: To diagnose complex tropical diseases in children
options.B: To prescribe medication during nursing staff shortages
options.C: To build cultural acceptance and reduce community resistance
options.D: To manage the financial accounts of the clinic

explanation: Community leaders hold great influence. Bringing them on board helps secure local backing and prevents cultural pushback against sensitive topics.

question: Which patient finding means you need to call for emergency help right away?

options.A: A heart rate of 102 beats per minute while walking
options.B: Blood pressure of 70/40 mmHg with altered mental status
options.C: Mild fatigue at the end of a normal daily work shift
options.D: Occasional fluttering sensations in the chest while resting

explanation: When blood pressure drops that low and the patient is confused, the bad rhythm is starving the brain and body of blood flow. That's an all-hands-on-deck emergency!

question: Which physical sign is a classic giveaway of an opioid overdose?

options.A: Wide dilated pupils
options.B: Pinpoint pupils
options.C: Severe hypertension
options.D: Extreme sweating

explanation: Opioids slow down the central nervous system. A classic clinical sign you'll learn to spot is profound sleepiness along with very tiny, constricted 'pinpoint' pupils.

question: What triggers hormone release during humoral stimulation?

options.A: Tropic hormones secreted by the anterior pituitary
options.B: Emotional stress and physical trauma responses
options.C: Changes in ion or nutrient levels in the blood
options.D: Direct electrical impulses sent from the brain

explanation: Humoral stimuli mean the glands are tasting the blood directly—like checking if there is too much sugar or calcium floating around.

question: What does the 'halo effect' mean during a performance appraisal?

options.A: Focusing only on mistakes made during the last week of the year
options.B: Rating every single staff member as average to keep the peace
options.C: Allowing one positive trait to result in an entirely high evaluation
options.D: Giving a nurse a poor review because of a single past argument

explanation: The halo effect happens when a nurse is so charming or great at one specific thing that the manager accidentally gives them top marks everywhere else, even where they need work.

question: What type of cells normally cover the outer part (ectocervix) of a healthy cervix?

options.A: Stratified squamous epithelium
options.B: Transitional epithelium
options.C: Simple columnar epithelium
options.D: Pseudostratified ciliated epithelium

explanation: The outer cervix is covered by tough stratified squamous cells. They act like a strong shield against friction and the natural acidity of the vagina.

question: What is a very common challenge when students have to grade their peers in clinicals?

options.A: Students may give inflated grades to friends due to leniency bias.
options.B: Students lack the physical ability to observe clinical skills.
options.C: Peer evaluation is strictly illegal in professional nursing programs.
options.D: It prevents students from ever working in healthcare teams.

explanation: Because we care about our friends, it can be really tough to give them a low score, which often leads to overly generous peer ratings!

question: Which type of tongue bumps (papillae) do NOT have any taste buds?

options.A: Filiform papillae
options.B: Fungiform papillae
options.C: Vallate papillae
options.D: Foliate papillae

explanation: Filiform papillae are the rough little bumps that give your tongue friction to help grip food—they aren't involved in tasting.

question: What is a direct way to check the quality of youth-friendly services from the clients' own viewpoint?

options.A: Counting the number of chairs in the parking lot
options.B: Gathering feedback through exit interviews and suggestion boxes
options.C: Reading national textbooks on adult medicine
options.D: Checking the personal financial records of the nursing staff

explanation: Spot on! Asking the young clients directly via suggestion boxes or quick chats lets you know what's working and what needs fixing.

question: What is the clear, dome-shaped structure at the very front of the eye that bends incoming light?

options.A: The tough sclera
options.B: The clear cornea
options.C: The pigmented iris
options.D: The sensitive retina

explanation: The cornea is the transparent front layer of the eye that first meets light and helps bend it toward the back. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h1)

question: If a patient misses work for weeks due to a hospital admission, how is their lost salary classified?

options.A: Indirect cost
options.B: Capital cost
options.C: Intangible cost
options.D: Direct medical cost

explanation: Indirect costs happen because illness stops someone from working. The hospital bill is direct, but the lost salary at their job is an indirect cost.

question: Which Nigerian agency is well known for regulating food and drug safety?

options.A: JAMB
options.B: NAFDAC
options.C: NYSC
options.D: FRSC

explanation: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) is our main regulatory body for food and drugs in Nigeria. Proudly Nigerian nursing knowledge!

question: In financial management, what is a "variance"?

options.A: The variation in patient recovery times across different wards
options.B: The difference between budgeted amounts and actual financial outcomes
options.C: The total amount of profit made from pharmacy sales alone
options.D: The legal penalty given to hospitals for missing safety records

explanation: A variance is simply the gap between what you planned to spend in your budget and what you actually spent in reality.

question: An elderly patient with arthritis uses a walking frame, but their small room is packed with heavy furniture. What should you do first?

options.A: Instruct the patient to stop using the walker immediately
options.B: Report the housing conditions to local law enforcement
options.C: Advise the patient to move to a skilled nursing facility today
options.D: Help rearrange and clear pathways to allow safe walker passage

explanation: Clearing pathways is a simple, practical step that immediately makes moving around safer without taking away the patient's independence.

question: Which of these nursing actions is a clear example of primary prevention focused on the host?

options.A: Screening blood samples for early signs of malaria
options.B: Providing physical therapy after a stroke
options.C: Treating severe complications in an intensive care unit
options.D: Administering routine childhood immunizations

explanation: Primary prevention stops disease before it even starts. Giving vaccines helps the body build a strong defense way ahead of any exposure.

question: Why is it better for nurses to advocate together through an organization rather than fighting alone at the bedside?

options.A: It removes the legal duty of care from individual practitioners
options.B: It prevents hospital management from ever questioning a nurse
options.C: It guarantees that all patient complaints are immediately dismissed
options.D: It gives nurses a stronger political voice to influence health laws

explanation: Politicians and policy-makers listen much more closely to an organized group representing thousands of healthcare workers than to a single voice!

question: Why is keeping a good energy balance important for your patients?

options.A: It keeps body weight and energy stores stable
options.B: It ensures the digestive tract never has to rest
options.C: It stops all cellular chemical reactions
options.D: It prevents the need for any physical activity

explanation: Energy balance just means calories in equal calories out. It is what stops a patient from experiencing sudden, unwanted weight changes.

question: What is a major goal of community mobilization when responding to an outbreak?

options.A: Encouraging citizens to avoid primary health clinics entirely
options.B: Punishing individuals who fall ill with the infectious disease
options.C: Empowering residents to adopt safe hygiene and sanitation practices
options.D: Eliminating the need for any future environmental sanitation

explanation: When communities are involved and empowered, they take charge of their own hygiene, making disease prevention much easier.

question: What is the main difference between a PET scan and a standard CT or MRI scan?

options.A: A PET scan takes only a few seconds while CT and MRI take hours.
options.B: A PET scan uses strong magnets while CT and MRI use radioactive dye.
options.C: A PET scan shows cellular function while CT and MRI mainly show body structures.
options.D: A PET scan is completely painless while CT and MRI cause physical discomfort.

explanation: You got it! PET scans look at how cells are working and using energy (metabolism), while regular scans like CT and MRI are more like cameras taking sharp pictures of your body's anatomy and physical structures.

question: What is the main goal of performing medication reconciliation?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of hospital pharmacy supplies
options.B: To test the memory of newly graduated nursing students
options.C: To avoid errors like missed doses, double dosing, and clashes
options.D: To force patients to buy their medications from the hospital

explanation: The core purpose is to catch and stop mistakes early, keeping your patient safe from harmful drug clashes. You're building solid clinical instincts!

question: Which service is especially helpful for giving family caregivers of individuals with ASD a much-needed break?

options.A: Respite care services
options.B: Sudden medication changes
options.C: Mandatory legal arbitration
options.D: Extended hospital admission

explanation: Spot on! Caring for someone full-time is heavy work. Respite care gives families a temporary break to rest and recharge.

question: What happens inside the body of a patient with severe burns that makes a high-protein diet critical for their survival?

options.A: Hypermetabolism causes rapid tissue breakdown and protein loss
options.B: Bones instantly release all stored calcium into the blood
options.C: The kidneys stop filtering waste products completely
options.D: The digestive tract absorbs fewer vitamins than normal

explanation: Severe burns put the body into an extreme 'overdrive' state where muscle and tissue break down rapidly. High protein helps fight off this severe wasting.

question: Which of these clinical actions goes against the rules of rational drug use?

options.A: Prescribing strong broad-spectrum antibiotics for a simple viral upper respiratory infection
options.B: Educating a diabetic patient on the correct technique for self-administering insulin
options.C: Administering a standard dose of paracetamol for a documented fever in an adult
options.D: Checking a patient's kidney function before starting a new maintenance medication

explanation: Remember: antibiotics fight bacteria, not viruses! Giving them for a simple cold or viral infection wastes medicine and causes drug resistance.

question: What is the name of the condition marked by lung inflammation and high white blood cells (eosinophils) when roundworm larvae travel through the lungs?

options.A: Nephrotic syndrome
options.B: Compartment syndrome
options.C: Cushing's syndrome
options.D: Loeffler's syndrome

explanation: Loeffler's syndrome happens when migrating parasite larvae cause temporary respiratory symptoms and changes in the lungs.

question: Genito-Pelvic Pain/Penetration Disorder mostly involves trouble with which of the following?

options.A: Vaginal penetration and associated pain
options.B: Controlling emotional attachment
options.C: Achieving a spike in blood pressure
options.D: Producing adequate testosterone levels

explanation: Easy peasy! The name tells the whole story: it groups together issues like painful intercourse, fear of pain, and tight pelvic muscles.

question: As a nurse, what is the very first thing you do after a patient's test comes back positive?

options.A: Discharge the patient to home isolation
options.B: Interview the index patient to find contacts
options.C: Vaccinating the entire neighborhood immediately
options.D: Closing down public markets in the local area

explanation: Spot on! We start by talking to the main patient (the index case) to gently find out who they've been hanging out with recently.

question: What is the primary reason for establishing trust during a genitourinary assessment?

options.A: To eliminate the requirement for formal medical documentation
options.B: To prevent the need for diagnostic laboratory tests
options.C: To speed up the physical examination process
options.D: To encourage the patient to share sensitive health details

explanation: Genitourinary symptoms involve private bodily functions, making trust essential for an honest and accurate patient history. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h1)

question: What age threshold is generally used to define a teenage bride?

options.A: Marriage before the onset of menarche
options.B: Marriage before the sixteenth birthday
options.C: Any marriage occurring while in secondary school
options.D: Marriage before the eighteenth birthday

explanation: Globally, a teenage bride is defined as any young girl who gets married before turning 18. Spotting this helps nurses identify vulnerable teens early!

question: A patient is fighting a bad malaria infection. Which food group should you encourage to boost their immune system?

options.A: Body-building foods like large amounts of table salt
options.B: Energy-giving foods like pure sugar and palm oil
options.C: Protective foods like oranges and spinach
options.D: Non-perishable foods like canned dry biscuits

explanation: Spot on! Fruits and veggies are 'protective' because their vitamins and minerals boost immunity and help the body fight off infections.

question: How does the medication simethicone help relieve gas?

options.A: It paralyzes the bowel muscles to stop cramping completely.
options.B: It neutralizes all stomach acid to prevent digestion.
options.C: It combines small gas bubbles into larger ones that are easier to expel.
options.D: It permanently stops all bacteria from living in the large intestine.

explanation: Simethicone is a neat little helper that rounds up tiny trapped gas bubbles into bigger ones so the body can pass them easily.

question: Why must researchers follow a standardized procedure during data collection?

options.A: To make the research process take longer
options.B: To avoid getting permission from the hospital
options.C: To ensure patients pay for their participation
options.D: To prevent outside disturbances from ruining results

explanation: Standardized procedures ensure every participant has the same experience, keeping data collection consistent and reliable. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h8)

question: How can severe anxiety or fear slow down a mother's labour?

options.A: It releases hormones that slow down or weaken uterine contractions.
options.B: It automatically dilates the cervix too quickly before the baby is ready.
options.C: It completely stops the maternal kidneys from producing urine.
options.D: It causes the baby to immediately turn into a breech position.

explanation: High stress floods the body with adrenaline (the fight-or-flight hormone), which can pump the brakes on smooth uterine contractions. Keeping mums calm is real nursing care!

question: Which of these is a very common female-related cause of infertility?

options.A: Permanent enlargement of the prostate gland
options.B: Hyperactive sperm motility within the uterus
options.C: Complete absence of the pituitary hormone testosterone
options.D: Tubal blockages from previous pelvic infections

explanation: Past untreated infections (like PID) can leave scars or blockages in the fallopian tubes, stopping the egg and sperm from meeting.

question: Which nursing action directly attacks a biological germ inside a patient's body?

options.A: Screening building ventilation systems
options.B: Teaching mothers how to wash their hands
options.C: Administering a prescribed course of antibiotics
options.D: Ensuring proper disposal of community waste

explanation: Medicines like antibiotics go right inside the patient to fight off and destroy the invading bacteria. Simple and direct!

question: What jelly-like structure in the inner ear gets pushed when moving fluid hits it during a head turn?

options.A: Otolith
options.B: Cupula
options.C: Tectorial membrane
options.D: Macula

explanation: The cupula acts just like a tiny swinging door inside your ear, moving whenever the fluid pushes against it. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h3)

question: How does the constant push for a male child indirectly cause higher rates of dangerous bleeding after birth?

options.A: It forces pregnant women to avoid attending antenatal care clinics entirely
options.B: It causes surgical instruments used during delivery to become contaminated
options.C: It restricts mothers from eating iron-rich foods after giving birth
options.D: It drives women to achieve grand multiparity, increasing uterine fatigue and bleeding risks

explanation: Trying over and over for a boy leads to many pregnancies, which wears out the womb muscles and raises the risk of severe bleeding after delivery.

question: What does the full circle of a pie chart stand for?

options.A: The total number of categories minus one
options.B: A total of 100 percent of a dataset
options.C: The average of all collected numbers
options.D: The median value of the research study

explanation: You've got this! Think of a whole pie representing everything you collected—that's always 100 percent.

question: What is the main job of the muscle layer in the ureter wall?

options.A: To filter waste products directly from tissue fluid
options.B: To secrete mucus that lubricates the inner lumen
options.C: To absorb excess water back into the bloodstream
options.D: To generate peristaltic waves that push urine down

explanation: Keep it up! The muscle squeezes in rhythmic waves (peristalsis) to gently milk the urine down into the bladder.

question: What is the very first thing public health teams do when investigating a suspected outbreak?

options.A: Impose a strict national travel lockdown
options.B: Write a final research paper for journals
options.C: Distribute free antibiotics to the public
options.D: Verify the diagnosis and confirm cases

explanation: Before jumping to conclusions, we always check with labs and clinics to make sure the reported illnesses are real and correctly diagnosed.

question: What happens to carbon dioxide during gas exchange in the lungs?

options.A: It moves from the pulmonary capillaries into the alveoli
options.B: It combines with oxygen to form a new nutrient compound
options.C: It binds tightly to hemoglobin inside the red blood cells
options.D: It is actively pumped from the alveoli into the bloodstream

explanation: Carbon dioxide travels from the blood in the capillaries across the membrane into the air sacs so it can leave the body through exhalation. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h4)

question: What do we call the process where cancer cells break away and spread through the blood or lymph to other parts of the body?

options.A: Mitosis
options.B: Metastasis
options.C: Metaplasia
options.D: Apoptosis

explanation: You're doing great! Metastasis happens when malignant cells travel via blood or lymph to set up secondary growths in distant organs.

question: What is a common dietary practice rooted in traditional African indigenous beliefs?

options.A: Total exclusion of all cooked vegetables from the diet
options.B: Consuming only imported foods during sacred ceremonies
options.C: Mandatory fasting for forty consecutive days each year
options.D: Avoiding specific foods that serve as family or clan totems

explanation: Many indigenous African traditions practice food taboos, avoiding certain plants or animals that connect to their ancestral clan totems.

question: What is the main goal of a nursing audit?

options.A: To evaluate and improve the quality of patient care
options.B: To punish nurses who make mistakes in documentation
options.C: To determine the monthly salary of nursing staff
options.D: To count the total number of hospital bed sheets

explanation: You've got this! Audits aren't witch hunts—they are helpful tools to check our care against set standards so we can find ways to do even better for our patients.

question: When we talk about 'social capital' in a community, what do we mean?

options.A: The trust and supportive networks built through social participation
options.B: The physical infrastructure of roads and water pipes
options.C: The total financial savings kept in local credit unions
options.D: The government grants given to public health clinics

explanation: Great thinking! Social capital is all about the strength of relationships, trust, and neighborly support in a community.

question: What does it mean when a nurse decides to 'cluster care' during a shift?

options.A: Grouping all patients with the same diagnosis in one bay
options.B: Doing several care tasks during one room visit to save time
options.C: Handing over multiple patients to a colleague all at once
options.D: Writing all patient charts at the very end of the shift

explanation: Spot on! Clustering care is a smart student trick: instead of walking in and out all day, you combine vitals, meds, and repositioning into one smooth bedside visit.

question: What happens to a woman's cervical mucus during her fertile window to help conception?

options.A: It becomes clear, stretchy, and slippery
options.B: It develops a foul odor and heavy discharge
options.C: It dries up completely to block germs
options.D: It turns thick, sticky, and brownish

explanation: High estrogen turns cervical mucus into a friendly, slippery highway that helps swimming sperm travel easily toward the egg. Nature is amazing!

question: Why does a nurse listen to the chest with a stethoscope during a respiratory assessment?

options.A: To detect normal breath sounds and abnormal adventitious sounds
options.B: To measure the exact blood pressure inside the lung tissue
options.C: To feel vibrations of the vocal cords through the chest wall
options.D: To check for skin temperature differences across the ribs

explanation: Auscultation allows the nurse to hear air moving through the airways and identify sounds like wheezes or crackles that indicate disease. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T2#GNS213_U2_T2_h3)

question: Through which part of the spinal cord do incoming sensory nerve signals enter?

options.A: Dorsal root
options.B: Lateral horn
options.C: Central canal
options.D: Ventral root

explanation: Sensory information always comes in through the back door—the dorsal root—bringing messages from the rest of the body into the central nervous system.

question: What happens when the lower oesophageal sphincter fails to close properly?

options.A: Air builds up rapidly in the upper airway
options.B: Digestive enzymes destroy the small intestine
options.C: Swallowed food gets trapped in the throat
options.D: Stomach acid flows backward into the tube

explanation: Think of this sphincter as a one-way gate. When it stays loose, irritating stomach contents can easily splash back upward, causing that familiar burning feeling.

question: Why might a bright, gifted child suddenly get poor grades on school tests?

options.A: A preference for learning physical skills over reading
options.B: An inability to process spoken instructions in class
options.C: Boredom from a lack of appropriate mental challenge
options.D: Severe physical fatigue caused by rapid growth spurts

explanation: It sounds surprising, but when schoolwork isn't challenging enough, brilliant kids get bored and check out. You're building solid nursing intuition!

question: What is the primary abnormal protein found in the red blood cells of a person with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Haemoglobin F
options.B: Haemoglobin C
options.C: Haemoglobin A
options.D: Haemoglobin S

explanation: The genetic mutation in sickle cell anaemia specifically leads to the production of abnormal haemoglobin S, which changes the shape of the red blood cells when it loses oxygen. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h1)

question: What is the main superpower of herd immunity in a community?

options.A: It ensures that all infectious agents mutate into harmless forms of microbes
options.B: It guarantees that every single person in the population will never get infected
options.C: It protects vulnerable individuals who cannot be vaccinated by breaking the transmission chain
options.D: It eliminates all environmental sources of bacteria within a specific geographical area

explanation: When almost everyone around is immune, the germ has nowhere to jump. This creates a protective shield around babies or sick folks who can't take vaccines.

question: Why do ethics committees carefully review a study's research objectives?

options.A: To decide which nursing journal will publish the final paper
options.B: To judge if the study poses any risks to participating patients
options.C: To calculate the total financial profit of the hospital
options.D: To verify the spelling and grammar of the title page

explanation: Ethics committees check your goals to ensure that whatever you plan to study is important enough to justify any potential burden on human participants. Patient safety always comes first! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h2)

question: What is the main goal of using the TNM staging system for lung cancer?

options.A: To determine the extent of disease spread and plan appropriate treatment
options.B: To measure the exact volume of air the lungs can hold
options.C: To calculate the patient's exact daily calorie requirements
options.D: To identify which specific type of cigarette the patient smoked

explanation: Brilliant! TNM helps the team figure out how big the tumor is, if it has reached lymph nodes, and how far it has spread, guiding the best treatment plan.

question: According to WHO guidelines, which condition is a strict medical reason (Category 4) NOT to use a progestin-only implant?

options.A: Controlled gestational diabetes
options.B: History of heavy menstrual periods
options.C: Mild uncomplicated hypertension
options.D: Current breast cancer

explanation: Active breast cancer is sensitive to hormones, making progestin implants unsafe (Category 4). Patient safety always comes first!

question: What is an urban 'food desert'?

options.A: A farming community that refuses to grow crops
options.B: A dry region where no humans live
options.C: An area lacking affordable and fresh whole foods
options.D: A marketplace that sells only drinking water

explanation: Food deserts are city neighborhoods where residents struggle to easily find and buy fresh, healthy food options.

question: Why is visiting a patient's home so helpful for disease management?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any medications.
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will never need a hospital visit.
options.C: It allows nurses to observe real-world habits and living conditions.
options.D: It places the entire workload on family members instead.

explanation: You get a true picture when you see where patients actually live! Home care lets you spot daily habits and environmental factors that directly affect their health.

question: What is a key piece of advice for a patient going home with a chronic bleeding disorder?

options.A: Recognize and report early signs of bleeding like unusual bruising or blood in the stool
options.B: Avoid drinking water entirely to prevent fluid overload in the blood vessels
options.C: Stop taking all prescribed medications once you feel a slight energy improvement
options.D: Engage in high-contact sports to build up your physical strength and endurance

explanation: Teaching patients to spot early warning signs means they can get help before a minor bleed turns into a major emergency.

question: Which cells in the testes are responsible for producing testosterone?

options.A: Spermatids
options.B: Leydig cells
options.C: Sertoli cells
options.D: Spermatogonia

explanation: Leydig cells are found between the tubules and synthesize the primary male sex hormone, testosterone. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h5)

question: What is the main drawback of using a 24-hour food recall to check what a patient eats?

options.A: It requires expensive laboratory equipment to calculate
options.B: Patients may forget or misreport what they actually ate
options.C: It only measures physical height rather than food
options.D: It takes over a week to complete a single interview

explanation: Memory can be tricky! Clients might easily forget that little afternoon snack or misjudge the size of their food portions.

question: What does the vital infection control rule 'one needle, one syringe, one time' mean for your daily practice?

options.A: Injection equipment must be used for only one patient and never reused
options.B: Syringes can be reused if they are washed with soap and water
options.C: Multiple patients can share a medication vial if a new needle is attached
options.D: Nurses should change needles between patients but keep the same syringe

explanation: It's simple and non-negotiable: a fresh, sterile needle and syringe for every single patient, every single time. You've got this rule down!

question: Which of these nursing duties counts as a skilled nursing intervention?

options.A: Managing complex wound care and dressing changes.
options.B: Assisting a resident with walking down the hallway.
options.C: Handing out meal trays to all residents at lunchtime.
options.D: Helping a resident put on their casual daytime clothes.

explanation: Wound care needs professional clinical technique and assessment, making it a true skilled nursing task!

question: When giving total care to a very ill patient, what is your absolute top priority?

options.A: Maintaining airway patency and breathing efficiency
options.B: Providing a full bath every morning
options.C: Encouraging heavy oral fluid intake
options.D: Ensuring clean bed linens and fresh hospital gowns

explanation: Oxygen is king! Keeping the airway clear is always priority number one because without oxygen, nothing else matters.

question: How does effective IEC help reduce the workload of overcrowded primary health clinics?

options.A: By convincing patients that they do not need to visit a nurse for minor symptoms
options.B: By automatically curing chronic diseases without the need for medication
options.C: By locking clinic doors on certain days of the week to force home remedies
options.D: By teaching people preventive habits and early care that stop mild illnesses from becoming severe

explanation: When communities practice prevention and seek early care, fewer people develop severe complications that require intensive clinic resources. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T2#GNS124_U5_T2_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a limitation or challenge of healthcare simulation?

options.A: Fitting simulation hours into a packed curriculum is difficult
options.B: Instructors need specialized training to run advanced scenarios properly
options.C: Mannequins cannot fully duplicate every emotional nuance of a real patient
options.D: Simulation successfully improves teamwork and reduces medical errors

explanation: Improving teamwork and reducing errors is a major benefit of simulation, not a limitation or challenge. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h7)

question: What is the most common immediate complication right after an FGM procedure?

options.A: Osteoporosis in later adulthood
options.B: Severe bleeding and acute pain
options.C: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Chronic hypertension

explanation: Spot on! Cutting sensitive genital tissue with basic tools typically causes immediate, heavy bleeding and intense pain.

question: Why do we call smooth muscle 'involuntary'?

options.A: It operates without conscious control from the brain
options.B: It cannot regenerate after an injury
options.C: It does not require any ATP to function
options.D: It lacks regular microscopic striations

explanation: Just like your heart beating while you sleep, smooth muscle works automatically behind the scenes without you having to think about it. Brilliant!

question: Why must a community health nurse look at both the environment and daily lifestyle of a population?

options.A: To trace the exact family tree of every community member
options.B: To understand the wide range of factors influencing public health
options.C: To fulfill government requirements for building new hospitals
options.D: To find out which residents have private health insurance

explanation: Spot on! People's health isn't just about germs; where they live, what they eat, and how they work all combine to shape their overall well-being.

question: Which of these charting entries is poorly written?

options.A: Wound measures 3 cm by 2 cm with no foul drainage
options.B: Patient slept quietly for four hours through the night
options.C: Patient walked 20 meters in the hallway with a walker
options.D: Patient appears to be in a very bad mood today

explanation: Correct! Vague labels like 'bad mood' are judgmental. Always write down the exact behaviors you observe instead.

question: What is a major social barrier that prevents Nigerian teenagers from seeking care?

options.A: Fear of community gossip and moral judgment from adults
options.B: Excessive availability of youth-only private hospitals everywhere
options.C: Mandatory free transport provided by local government councils
options.D: Strict laws requiring teenagers to study nursing in secondary school

explanation: Cultural stigma and the fear of being judged or gossiped about in the community stop many young people from visiting clinics. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T4#GNS312_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which cranial nerve transmits sensory signals for the sense of smell from the nose to the brain?

options.A: Cranial Nerve I (Olfactory nerve)
options.B: Cranial Nerve V (Trigeminal nerve)
options.C: Cranial Nerve II (Optic nerve)
options.D: Cranial Nerve VII (Facial nerve)

explanation: Cranial nerve I, the olfactory nerve, carries smell sensations straight from the nasal roof into the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why do health programs often fail when they are imposed from the outside without community involvement?

options.A: They fail to match cultural realities and local priorities
options.B: Governments never allow outsiders to visit villages
options.C: Local health workers refuse to touch foreign supplies
options.D: They always cost too much money to run

explanation: Interventions that ignore local values and real community needs lack ownership and fail to gain public trust. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the main goal of prescribing a beta-blocker for someone with angina?

options.A: Dissolving blood clots inside the coronary arteries
options.B: Widening narrowed airways in the lung tissues
options.C: Immediate relief of a sudden acute heart attack
options.D: Long-term prevention of chest pain episodes

explanation: Beta-blockers are like the steady guardians taken every day to keep future chest pain away by calming down the heart's workload.

question: Which safety principle describes an organization that treats a tiny slip-up as an urgent warning sign?

options.A: Reluctance to simplify
options.B: Commitment to resilience
options.C: Preoccupation with failure
options.D: Deference to expertise

explanation: Being 'preoccupied with failure' just means staying alert to small near-misses instead of brushing them off!

question: Which grade of moulding describes skull bones that overlap firmly but can still be separated by finger pressure?

options.A: Grade 3 moulding
options.B: Grade 1 moulding
options.C: Grade 4 moulding
options.D: Grade 0 moulding

explanation: Grade 1 means the bones overlap slightly but remain reducible with gentle pressure. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h3)

question: What is an important final step after finishing an eye irrigation for a chemical burn?

options.A: Rechecking the tear pH to ensure it has returned to normal
options.B: Rinsing the patient's entire face with rubbing alcohol
options.C: Instructing the patient to avoid blinking for two hours
options.D: Applying a tight eye patch with heavy pressure tape

explanation: Checking the pH one last time confirms that all the harmful chemical has been fully neutralized and washed away. Great wrap-up!

question: In midwifery, what is the medical term for a normal, uncomplicated vaginal delivery?

options.A: Dystocia
options.B: Cephalopelvic disproportion
options.C: Placenta praevia
options.D: Eutocia

explanation: You'll often hear 'eutocia' used to describe a smooth, straightforward birth with no major hitches. It's the exact opposite of dystocia!

question: What is a main reason fresh fruits spoil so fast after harvest in hot climates?

options.A: Excessive consumption of vegetables by local farmers
options.B: Inadequate cold storage and refrigeration facilities
options.C: Overly strict international export quality standards
options.D: The use of organic seeds instead of commercial hybrids

explanation: Correct! Without good refrigeration in hot weather, fresh produce unfortunately goes bad before it ever gets to market.

question: Which part of the brain is mainly responsible for sensing fear and emotional threats?

options.A: The pituitary gland
options.B: The cerebellum
options.C: The amygdala
options.D: The medulla oblongata

explanation: Think of the amygdala as your brain's personal security alarm. It picks up on emotional threats and kicks off that familiar fear response.

question: How does widespread tobacco use create a double challenge for Nigeria's health system?

options.A: It reduces the overall population so much that clinics have no patients to treat
options.B: It causes nurses to leave public clinics for international job opportunities
options.C: It forces hospitals to buy expensive imported equipment for infectious diseases only
options.D: It requires managing rising lifestyle diseases alongside existing infectious disease challenges

explanation: Clinics have to juggle treating traditional infectious diseases while also handling a growing wave of chronic illnesses caused by tobacco. You are learning fast!

question: A nurse receives a batch of donated nutrition teaching materials from an NGO. What is the best way to use them?

options.A: Give them all to private doctors in the city center
options.B: Integrate them into daily antenatal health talks and clinic education
options.C: Throw them away because they did not come from the ministry
options.D: Lock them away in a drawer until the NGO supervisor visits

explanation: Brilliant! Donated materials are most helpful when put straight into daily clinic activities like antenatal talks to educate mothers. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h7)

question: Which eye condition mainly causes a loss of straight-ahead or central vision due to damage to the macula?

options.A: Chronic open-angle glaucoma
options.B: Senile cataracts
options.C: Diabetic retinopathy
options.D: Age-Related Macular Degeneration

explanation: Spot on! Age-Related Macular Degeneration specifically targets the macula, affecting the center of a person's visual field.

question: What is the main reason for putting matching ID bands on a newborn before they leave the delivery room?

options.A: To keep track of feeding schedules in the nursery
options.B: To monitor circulation in the distal extremities
options.C: To track the baby's daily weight changes accurately
options.D: To prevent infant mix-ups and ensure secure identification

explanation: Safety first! Matching ID bands ensure the baby always stays correctly linked to their mother without any mix-ups.
